candidate_profile.description: The candidate immediately focuses on the right problem, structures the diagnosis sharply, uses the urban versus suburban split intelligently, identifies the assortment mismatch, and gives a crisp recommendation grounded in customer behavior, profitability, and store economics.
behaviour_rules: Start with a concise recap and explicitly state that the issue is likely on the revenue side because major backend cost savings have already been captured.
Ask two or three focused, hypothesis-driven questions on store profitability variation, consumer behavior, and competitive differences across metropolitan and suburban stores.
Use a clear, prioritized framework centered on geography, customer behavior, and product mix.
Quickly test and deprioritize competition once the facts indicate it is proportionally similar across areas.
Recognize that a uniform product mix across all 15 stores is likely inefficient if customer needs differ by geography.

Clearly explain that suburban customers buy more major appliances and electronics, which are higher-margin categories, while urban customers skew toward clothing, smaller furniture, and smaller appliances.
Conclude that urban stores are not aligned to local demand and are losing both revenue and floor-space productivity.
Give a crisp recommendation to analyze customer behavior store by store, localize assortment, and consider closure of stores that cannot sustain a lower-value mix.

expected_issues: May not quantify the economic upside explicitly because the case is primarily diagnostic rather than numerical.
Could still be challenged for a more detailed rollout plan across stores, though the core recommendation should be excellent.
expected_feedback_points: Excellent focus on revenue rather than cost.
Excellent structure around store geography, customer behavior, and product mix.
Correct rejection of competition as the main root cause.
Excellent diagnosis that the same assortment is better suited to suburban than urban demand.
Clear linkage between suburban profitability and higher-margin major appliances and electronics.
Excellent recommendation to localize assortment and consider closure where economics do not work.
